source.original_title: 05/08/2026 - Fredilito Abejon & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/08/2026 - Fredilito Abejon & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Closed

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Named twice by the prospect: 'when I spoke with Kim previously, I told him that I just started a new job' and 'like I was telling Kim, you know, I'm willing to, once I get the road map, travel with the kettlebells in my trunk'. Note the prospect refers to Kim as 'him', matching the Soneel Raj call the previous day.

prospect.name: Fredilito Abejon
prospect.aka: Goes by Fred — asked the rep to use it
prospect.occupation: Longshoreman in maritime transportation — loading and unloading container ships, barges and cruise ships for contracted companies. Previously worked in construction. Waited six years on supplemental status before securing a full-time slot. Rotating three-week shift cycles, currently nights, up to seven days a week and 10-hour days, with schedules confirmed only the day before. Military veteran.
prospect.family_status: Married; wife currently living in the Philippines and he is working to bring her to the US. Planning to use his VA loan to buy a home for them.
prospect.training_background: Was doing calisthenics and training consistently in the latter half of last year, including supplementation, and reports feeling good then; has not trained since. Hired a personal trainer twice — around $500 the first time — specifically to prepare for the longshore physical agility test, which he passed on both occasions. Tried one of Trevor's short lymphatic routines and liked it. No kettlebell experience.
prospect.medical: Sprained his lower back at work approximately one month before this call — right side first, then the left side the following week — and describes being in a lot of pain at the time. Under active chiropractic care, described as on and off, and attended a chiropractor appointment immediately before this call. Also attends employer-funded Stretch Lab sessions, one of which he had also just come from. Reports being physically 'bounced around a lot' by the suspension of the yard vehicles he drives, which he says compounds the back problem. Has been made ill three times by poor air quality in those vehicles and now wears a respirator. Reports accumulated aches, pains and probable inflammation.

signals: Explicitly preservation rather than gain: 'at this point, I'm beyond aesthetics, you know, just trying to preserve my health, my muscle strength, cardio, you know, for the job'
Older and already medically managed — active chiropractic care plus employer-funded Stretch Lab sessions, both attended on the day of the call
Reasonable earned income with almost no discretionary liquidity: around $5,000 in the account on payday, roughly $2,000 monthly disposable, no credit card and a damaged credit score
The goal is holding on to working capacity for a defined period — ten more years to vest a pension and free medical cover for himself and his wife
Framing is functional and unsentimental: keeping up with the younger workers, handling the rigours of the job, avoiding further injury

Distinguished from the_prehab_fighter because the back sprain is an occupational injury rather than a serious active health event, and from the_rebuilder because he is defending current function rather than reclaiming a former self

goals.text: Preserve and improve strength, stamina and cardio specifically to handle the physical demands of longshore work
Stop getting injured — the back sprains are new and did not happen before
Stay working ten more years to vest a company pension and free medical cover for himself and his wife
Keep up with, and outperform, the younger workers on the job
Get on a regimented mobility and stretching programme rather than relying on ad hoc sessions
Enter his 60s feeling young rather than declining — 'I'm not going into my 60s. Like, I'm still young.'
Improve overall quality of life, which he says he does not have right now
Train portably — kettlebells in the car boot, worked around unpredictable shifts and locations
Be physically able to keep earning so he can bring his wife to the US and buy a home on his VA loan

pains.text: Sprained his lower back at work about a month ago, both sides in consecutive weeks, and is in ongoing chiropractic care
Getting injured in ways that never used to happen — 'the body is still aging faster than what I am comfortable with'
Vehicle suspension bounces him around all shift and compounds the back problem
Made ill three times by poor air quality in the yard vehicles
Rotating three-week shift cycles including nights, up to 10-hour days seven days a week, with schedules confirmed only the day before
Stopped training and stopped supplementation, and links that directly to how he now feels
Overwhelmed by conflicting fitness information — 'there's so much information out there and a lot of it's good information, but then it's like hit and miss'
No accountability and no feedback when training alone
Damaged credit score with no credit card, paying roughly $1,000 a month for two more months to a credit-repair programme that already cost around $6,000
Spent around $7,000 in December repairing his van
Being ribbed by younger colleagues on the job
Separated from his wife, who is in the Philippines

objections.raw_quote: shoot, is, is, is any of those levels of, I mean, because I don't have that kind of, like, saving for disposable income. Is there any of those, uh, can be, like, into, like, payment plans or?
objections.rep_response: Confirmed plans exist — 'Of course, man. You know, not everyone's going to be able to pay this up front' — then asked which tier he was leaning toward before establishing anything about his finances.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, it's still kind of steep. I mean, I make the money right now, but I'm still trying to like... Let's see, if $4,000 divided by $3,000, that'd be like $1,000... But if you can work with me and like, if I can do like a monthly for the duration of, you know, the period, I can swing that absolutely.
objections.rep_response: Sought permission for financial questions, then took cash on hand, disposable income, credit cards and credit score. Then offered a six-payment structure described as something not normally permitted.

objections.raw_quote: okay, fine and dandy, you know, Trevor, you has this program all that stuff. But then, you know, I think he's in his 40s? So, you know, how, how does he know what somebody in their 50s, 60s or 70s or beyond, you know, how can he formulate?
objections.rep_response: Answered with an unevidenced experience claim — 'Through experience. He's been doing this for 10 years. All age groups, of all demographics' — and then 'At the end of the day, we're all human.' No age-group testimonials were shown, despite the prospect having just asked to see some.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Three separate instalment structures were quoted, each carrying an undisclosed uplift over the list price and none described as a finance charge. Twelve months: six payments of $1,800, total $10,800 against a $9,000 list price — a $1,800 uplift, and the only total the rep volunteered, and only after being asked. Six months: six payments of $1,200, total $7,200 against a $6,000 list price — a $1,200 uplift, and the total was never stated by the rep; the prospect computed it himself. Three months: three payments of $1,500, total $4,500 against a $4,000 list price — a $500 uplift, total never stated. The rep characterised the uplift only as 'It will be slightly more expensive because we're spreading it out.' He also stated the plan length was an exception: 'Typically, we're not meant to do this. The maximum payments we can do is three, but we can stretch that out to six months for you.' A payoff concession was offered verbally: 'if you want to pay it off sooner, we'll honor the original amount for yourself.'
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Upgrade credit only: 'if you want to do another six months with us, we just charge you the difference as opposed to another 6k.' When the prospect asked whether the difference was calculated against $9,000 or $10,800, the rep said $9,000, making the top-up $3,000. No refund, guarantee or cancellation terms were mentioned at any point.

evidence: Explicit tier selection and agreement: 'As much as I do the 12, I think I'm going to go with the six grand' and 'So my first move is going be 1200 then... And then monthly, monthly?... Okay. Yeah. I can pull that off.'
Rep confirmed: 'All right, man. Let's do it.'
Prospect asked for the paperwork — 'So you're going to send me the contract and all that stuff?' — and the rep said he would walk him through it
Counter-evidence: the rep then said 'First thing I'll do, Fred. I'll remove my note taker' and the recording ends, so no payment, contract or signature is witnessed

Counter-evidence and material: on the Roy Norman call two days earlier the same rep removed the notetaker after an equally explicit yes and the deal then collapsed off-record, as he later admitted to his manager. This close carries the same unverifiable risk and should be reconciled against the payment processor
Pre-offer commitment was genuinely strong — he rated trust in the programme a flat 10 out of 10 before any price was mentioned, the only 10 in this batch
outcome.cash_collection_basis: payment_plan_total — six monthly payments of $1,200 for the six-month programme. Note this is $1,200 above the $6,000 list price for the same tier. Only the first $1,200 payment was in prospect at the point the recording stopped, and no payment was witnessed.
outcome.next_step: Rep to send the contract and process the first $1,200 payment, then presumably book the Trevor onboarding call. None of this is on the recording.

notable.note: Two findings dominate this call. First, the prospect sprained his lower back at work about a month earlier — both sides in consecutive weeks — is under active chiropractic care, and came to this call directly from a chiropractor appointment which he mentioned in his first thirty seconds. He was then sold a loaded ballistic kettlebell programme and nobody asked whether his chiropractor had cleared him for it, what the diagnosis was, or whether the injury had resolved. The rep instead used the back as a selling point: 'What are your limitations in your body, such as your lower back that you mentioned?' Second, all three instalment structures quoted carry roughly a 12-20% uplift over the list price with no finance charge, rate or fee ever named — the six-month tier moves from $6,000 to $7,200 and the prospect worked that total out himself because the rep never stated it. This was structured for a man who had just disclosed no credit card, a damaged credit score, an existing $1,000-a-month obligation to a credit-repair company for two more months, and around $2,000 of monthly disposable income. At $1,200 a month the plan absorbs 60% of his disposable income, and for the first two months his committed outgoings exceed it. Nobody did that arithmetic on the call.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion throughout, including most of the pillar delivery and the entire financial-questioning sequence, where the rep's questions and the prospect's answers alternate under the wrong labels. Roles resolved from content. The prospect's arithmetic at 00:39:20 and 00:45:08 is garbled by the transcription (dollar signs inserted into division statements), but the figures reconcile: three payments of $1,500 on the three-month tier, six of $1,200 on the six-month, six of $1,800 on the twelve-month. Recording is deliberately terminated by the rep before the contract and payment, for the third time in this batch.
